idiom_name: Slick MappedColumnType.base / custom ColumnType mapping the entity to JSON
implementation_notes: Slick core has no JSON column, so the pattern is completed by hand: declare the column as its stored representation (String/TEXT, or a jsonb column cast on read) and publish an implicit mapper - MappedColumnType.base[Details, String](encode, decode), or a full ColumnType with GetResult/SetParameter - while play-json or circe does the actual serialization. Once the implicit is in scope the column behaves like any built-in type in queries. Hand-written mapping is the honest classification because every serialized type and every query site repeats the exercise, and libraries that map columns explicitly rather than by derived codecs demand the same instances.
pitfalls: A missing implicit mapper is a compile error at the query site, and importing it at the wrong scope is the usual cause.
The mapped representation must match the physical column: a jsonb column read as String needs an explicit cast or the driver rejects the type.
Throwing inside the decoder turns a bad historical payload into an exception on read; model the failure (Either) where rows are long-lived.
